claims.text: Hoffmann et al. trained 400+ language models and found that for compute-optimal training, model size and training tokens should be scaled equally at roughly 20 tokens per parameter. Chinchilla (70B parameters, 1.4 trillion tokens) outperformed Gopher (280B parameters) and other larger models on identical compute budgets, proving prior scaling practices that maximized parameters while limiting data were severely suboptimal.
